steps: Oxygen is used in aerobic respiration to break down glucose completely.
It combines with hydrogen to form water, allowing the release of energy.
Carbon dioxide and water are the end products of aerobic respiration.
items.finalAnswer: Oxygen enables the complete breakdown of glucose during aerobic respiration, releasing energy and producing carbon dioxide and water.

steps: Aerobic respiration is the breakdown of food in the presence of oxygen to release energy.
Anaerobic respiration is the breakdown of food in the absence of oxygen to release energy.
items.finalAnswer: Aerobic respiration occurs in the presence of oxygen, whereas anaerobic respiration occurs in its absence.

steps: In animals, anaerobic respiration produces lactic acid.
In yeast, anaerobic respiration produces ethanol and carbon dioxide.
items.finalAnswer: Animals produce lactic acid; yeast produces ethanol and carbon dioxide.

steps: During intense exercise, the muscles may not receive enough oxygen for their energy needs.
Muscle cells then respire anaerobically and produce lactic acid.
The accumulation of lactic acid can cause muscle fatigue and cramps.
items.finalAnswer: When oxygen is deficient, muscles respire anaerobically, producing lactic acid that may cause fatigue and cramps.

steps: Energy from respiration is used for muscle contraction and movement.
It is used for active transport of substances across cell membranes.
It is used to make new molecules and for growth and repair.
It is used in cell division and other activities of cells.
items.finalAnswer: Respiratory energy powers movement, active transport, synthesis, growth, repair, and cell division.

steps: ATP (adenosine triphosphate) is the chief energy currency of all cells.
Energy released during respiration is used to form ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate: ADP + phosphate + energy → ATP.
ATP stores energy in its chemical bonds and transfers it to cellular activities when required.
When ATP breaks down into ADP and phosphate, energy is released: ATP → ADP + phosphate + energy.
items.finalAnswer: ATP stores and transfers energy for cellular activities, so it is called the chief energy currency of cells.

steps: Chlorophyll in the leaves absorbs light energy from the Sun.
Light energy is converted into chemical energy.
Water is split into hydrogen and oxygen; oxygen is released.
Hydrogen combines with carbon dioxide to form glucose.
items.finalAnswer: In photosynthesis, chlorophyll captures light energy, which is used to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water, releasing oxygen.

steps: Carbon dioxide enters the leaves from the air through small openings called stomata.
Water is absorbed from the soil by the roots, mainly through root hairs.
The water is transported from the roots to the leaves through xylem vessels.
items.finalAnswer: Plants take in carbon dioxide through leaf stomata and absorb water through their roots, which transport it to the leaves.
